<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-summary">Summary</button></h2><div id="work-acc-summary" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Alaṅkāramañjarī is a treatise on poetics which is divided into 20 chapters and discusses various literary devices and figures of speech, providing examples of their usage in poetry. It covers a wide range of topics including metaphor, simile, irony, hyperbole, and puns. Alaṅkāramañjarī is written in a simple and accessible style, making it a useful resource for students of Sanskrit literature. One notable feature of Alaṅkāramañjarī is its focus on the practical application of literary devices, with Ruyyaka providing many examples from famous works of poetry to illustrate his points. The work is also known for its clear and concise explanations of complex concepts, making it a valuable resource for anyone seeking to improve their understanding of Sanskrit poetics.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contents">Contents</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contents" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">Alaṅkāramañjarī is a comprehensive treatise on poetics, covering a wide range of topics related to literary devices and figures of speech. The work is divided into 20 chapters, each focusing on a particular aspect of poetic expression. Some of the key topics covered in the work include:<br>1. Introduction: Ruyyaka begins the work with an overview of the importance of studying poetics and an explanation of the scope of the work.<br>2. Definition of Alaṅkāra: This chapter provides a definition of the term &quot;alaṅkāra&quot; and discusses its various types.<br>3. Definition of Artha: This chapter defines the term &quot;artha&quot; (meaning) and its various types.<br>4. Definition of Śabda: This chapter defines the term &quot;Śabda&quot; (word) and its various types.<br>5. Definition of Rasa: This chapter defines the term &quot;rasa&quot; (sentiment) and its various types.<br>6. Definition of Dhvani: This chapter discusses the concept of &quot;dhvani&quot; (suggestion) and its various types.<br>7. Metaphor: This chapter discusses the use of metaphor in poetry and provides examples of its usage.<br>8. Simile: This chapter discusses the use of simile in poetry and provides examples of its usage.<br>9. Irony: This chapter discusses the use of irony in poetry and provides examples of its usage.<br>10. Hyperbole: This chapter discusses the use of hyperbole in poetry and provides examples of its usage.<br>11. Puns: This chapter discusses the use of puns in poetry and provides examples of its usage.<br>12. Upamāna: This chapter discusses the concept of &quot;Upamāna&quot; (comparison) and its various types.<br>13. Vyañjana: This chapter discusses the concept of &quot;Vyañjana&quot; (suggestion) and its various types.<br>14. Anuprāsa: This chapter discusses the use of &quot;Anuprāsa&quot; (repetition of consonant sounds) in poetry.<br>15. Alaṅkāra in different genres of poetry: This chapter discusses the application of Alaṅkāras in different genres of poetry such as epic, lyric, and drama.<br>16. Rasas and their combinations: This chapter discusses the different rasas (sentiments) and their combinations.<br>17. Different types of Alaṅkāras and their applicability: This chapter discusses the various types of Alaṅkāras and their applicability.<br>18. Guṇa, Doṣa, and the evaluation of poetry: This chapter discusses the concepts of guṇa (merit) and doṣa (defect) in poetry and provides a framework for evaluating poems.<br>19. Poetic expression in drama: This chapter discusses the use of poetic expression in drama and provides examples of its usage.<br>20. Conclusion: The final chapter provides a summary of the key concepts discussed in the work and emphasizes the importance of studying poetics for the development of poetic skill.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-uniqueness">Uniqueness</button></h2><div id="work-acc-uniqueness" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">The uniqueness of the &quot;Alaṅkāramañjarī&quot; lies in its comprehensive treatment of various figures of speech and its organization of these figures into chapters according to their types. It not only provides examples for each figure of speech but also classifies them into various subtypes, making it a valuable resource for poets and scholars studying Sanskrit literature. Additionally, the work includes discussions on the use of figures of speech in different types of compositions, such as poetry and prose, and the effect they have on the reader or listener. Its detailed analysis and explanation of figures of speech make it an essential work in the field of Sanskrit literary criticism.</div></div></div>
<div class="accordion-item"><h2 class="accordion-header"><button class="accordion-button collapsed" type="button" data-bs-toggle="collapse" data-bs-target="#work-acc-contribution">Contribution &amp; Notes</button></h2><div id="work-acc-contribution" class="accordion-collapse collapse"><div class="accordion-body">&quot;Alaṅkāramañjarī&quot; is a significant contribution to Sanskrit literature as it provides a comprehensive and systematic treatment of figures of speech, or Alaṅkāras. It is an invaluable resource for scholars and poets studying Sanskrit literature, as it not only identifies different types of figures of speech but also classifies them into subtypes and provides numerous examples for each. The work is also notable for its discussion of the appropriate use of figures of speech in various types of compositions, such as poetry and prose, and their effect on the reader or listener. Its detailed analysis and explanation of Alaṅkāras have greatly influenced subsequent works on Sanskrit literary criticism, making it an essential and enduring contribution to the field.<br><br>Alaṅkāramañjarī of Rājānaka Ruyyaka is considered an important text in the field of Sanskrit poetics and rhetoric. It is known for its comprehensive treatment of various figures of speech and poetic devices, including the use of metaphor, simile, hyperbole, and irony. The work also presents a detailed analysis of the different forms and styles of Sanskrit poetry, including epic, lyric, and drama. In addition, Alaṅkāramañjarī contains numerous examples of these devices from various works of Sanskrit literature, making it a valuable resource for students and scholars of Sanskrit poetry.</div></div></div>
